reading.body:
NTT's Ashburn VA4 data center publishes 32 MW of IT capacity, accounting for roughly 2.4 percent of the 1,326 MW across Virginia facilities that have disclosed their power budgets.

At standard densities, 32 MW can support between 800 racks for AI training workloads (40 kW per rack) or 3,200 racks for traditional colocation (10 kW per rack). The operator has not published either figure, so the true hardware footprint depends on tenant workload composition. This gap between power and rack count is not incidental, it is the distinction between AI-dense infrastructure and general-purpose colocation.

The facility sits inside Ashburn's data center corridor, one of Virginia's densest concentrations of published capacity. The state has 326 mapped facilities in total, but only 19 have published megawatt figures. This means 1,326 MW is a floor for Virginia's installed capacity, not a ceiling. The vast majority of the state's infrastructure remains dark to public measurement.

The operator has not published grid interconnection details, power pricing, or tenant identity. No certifications appear in the published specifications. Whether this facility runs AI workloads, balances other compute, or serves traditional colocation cannot be read from available data.
